posts.title: Here I Am, Here I Am
posts.excerpt: God is not the one who is far. He is not the one hiding. He is not the one refusing to be found. He is standing there saying, here I am, here I am, to a whole nation that will not even turn its head.
posts.description: God is not the one who is far. He is standing there saying here I am to a whole nation that will not even turn its head. The distance is not on His end.

posts.title: When He Called, They Did Not Answer
posts.excerpt: Reading Isaiah, you feel the two sides of God almost verse by verse. One moment He is inviting. The next moment He is warning. Both are Him. That is not a contradiction. It is who He is.
posts.description: God calls and calls. But there is a point where the ignoring itself becomes the judgment. Isaiah shows both sides of God almost verse by verse.

posts.title: Find One
posts.excerpt: This whole verse is God essentially saying, find one. Find one just and honest person in this whole city, and I will spare it. One. That is all He is asking for.
posts.description: God told Jeremiah to search Jerusalem for even one just and honest person, and He would spare the city. One faithful life carries more weight than we realize.

posts.title: He Wants Us
posts.excerpt: Activity gives us something to measure. Sacrifices could be counted. Boxes could be checked. At the end of the day, they had something to point to. Relationship is harder to measure.
posts.description: God told Israel the sacrifices were never the point. What He wanted was them. It is still easy to substitute activity for relationship.

posts.title: Position Doesn't Equal Proximity
posts.excerpt: We should not assume that just because someone leads in a church, they are close to God. Some are. Some aren't. Position doesn't equal proximity.
posts.description: Pashhur was the priest in charge of the temple, and he had God's prophet arrested and beaten. You can hold a position of spiritual leadership and still not know His voice.

posts.title: As Sure As Sure Gets
posts.excerpt: God doesn't need to add weight. His word already carries all the weight in the universe. When He swears by His own name, He's not trying to convince anyone. He's just underlining the certainty of what He's saying.
posts.description: God swears by His own name in this verse, and Jesus told us not to swear at all. The difference is that God has never once needed to add weight to His word.

posts.title: Have Any of Them Listened
posts.excerpt: A different kind of false prophet than Jeremiah was dealing with, but the root is the same. Speaking for God without ever standing before God.
posts.description: Jeremiah stops mid-rebuke to ask whether any of the prophets had actually been in God's presence. It is an easier question to dodge now than it has ever been.

posts.title: Careful With His Name
posts.excerpt: Because my emotions and feelings had lied to me. What I thought was a clear word from the Lord turned out to be my own hopes wearing a spiritual label.
posts.description: God tells them to stop saying 'prophecy from the Lord' when they are really giving authority to their own ideas. Putting His name on our own hopes is easier to do than we think.

posts.title: Ten Days
posts.excerpt: Ten days can feel like an eternity in a hard situation. When you're scared, when decisions need to be made, waiting even a few hours for clarity feels impossible.
posts.description: The people came to Jeremiah in crisis and promised to obey whatever God said. He made them wait ten days before He answered.

posts.title: Even This Morning
posts.excerpt: That's where faithfulness gets learned. Not on the far side of the hard thing, but right in the middle of it.
posts.description: Jeremiah writes this from the far side of the worst thing that ever happened to him. The harder question is whether we can say it while we are still in the middle of it.

posts.title: Depending or Managing
posts.excerpt: Most of the time I'm not really depending. I'm managing. Handling. Capable. Asking Him to help me pull off my own plan instead of asking Him what His plan actually is.
posts.description: Two words in this verse ask something of us. Depending is not the same as managing, and searching is not the same as hoping.

posts.title: Was Your Faith Deeper This Year Than Last Year?
posts.excerpt: Most of us drift into a new year without really stopping to look at the one behind us. Did I grow? Or did I just get older?
posts.description: A new year is one of the rare pauses where we get to ask whether we grew or just got older. Five things to sit down with before you plan anything else.

posts.title: Not Abandoned Forever
posts.excerpt: That's the part we forget in a hard season. When life gets heavy and God feels quiet, the temptation is to assume He's walked away. He hasn't.
posts.description: When He's correcting us, it's because He loves us, not because He's done with us.

posts.title: Fear Isn't Love
posts.excerpt: We're supposed to speak truth. A lot of us soften it because we're scared of how people will react, and then we call that softening love. It's not love. It's fear.
posts.description: A lot of us soften the truth because we're scared of how people will react, and then we call it love. God told Ezekiel not to be afraid of the nettles.

posts.title: Let It Sink In First
posts.excerpt: We're fast to tell everyone else what they should be hearing from God. What we don't like is slowing down and letting God's words land on us first.
posts.description: Before Ezekiel says a word to anyone else, God tells him to let His words sink into his own heart first.

posts.title: When the Wait Makes Us Casual
posts.excerpt: Just because something hasn't happened yet doesn't mean it isn't going to. God doesn't move by our calendar. His delays aren't denials.
posts.description: Israel had a saying: time passes, and prophecies come to nothing. We do the same thing when the wait gets long.

posts.title: Nobody Else's Faith Can Save You
posts.excerpt: Being from a Christian family doesn't cover you. Being a good person doesn't cover you. The gap between knowing about God and knowing Him is bigger than we like to admit.
posts.description: Even Noah, Daniel, and Job couldn't save anyone but themselves. Every person has to deal with God for themselves.

posts.title: Running on Our Own Power
posts.excerpt: Most of us settle for the version of our life we can produce on our own. We get competent and capable, and good at making things happen. Somewhere in there, we stop noticing that we've been running on our own power for a long time.
posts.description: Jerusalem started thinking the fame and the beauty were her own, and forgot who gave it to her. Most of us settle for the life we can produce on our own.

posts.title: Who Are You Blaming?
posts.excerpt: As long as we're pointing at someone else for why our life is the way it is, we're stuck. Nothing can change. We've handed the keys to our own life over to somebody else.
posts.description: Israel had a saying about sour grapes and blaming the generation before. God tells them each person stands before Him on their own.

posts.title: Faithful, Not Understood
posts.excerpt: When God asks you to speak, your job isn't to make sure everyone understands. Your job is to be faithful with what He gave you. How it lands is between them and the Lord.
posts.description: Ezekiel was told he only talks in riddles. When God asks you to speak, your job is to be faithful, not to make sure everyone understands.

posts.title: He Knows Your Evening Too
posts.excerpt: Ezekiel didn't get a timeline. He just kept walking in obedience, and then one evening God moved. He had the timing of the whole thing in His hand the entire time.
posts.description: Ezekiel lived mostly silent for years, then God gave him his voice back the night before the news arrived. God has the timing of the whole thing in His hand.
